traits: Dark brown to chocolate-brown cap, 5 to 20 cm, dry, velvety
Yellow tubes; fine blood-red to orange-red pores that turn strongly blue when pressed
Thick stem, 5 to 15 cm, yellow under fine bright red dots: dots, not a net
Bright yellow, firm flesh that turns strongly blue when cut (the blue fades within an hour or a few) · mild taste
Broadleaf and conifer woods, non-chalky soil · June to November
safetyNote: Eat only well cooked: raw or undercooked it causes gastroenteritis, and Tox Info Suisse asks for at least 20 minutes of cooking. A stem with red dots and no net is the main feature that sets it apart from Satan’s bolete and several other toxic red boletes, whose stem has a net.
